subject: Recap & asks: burst profile, streaming constraints, and next steps
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@vendipay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & asks: burst profile, streaming constraints, and next steps

Hi Olivia — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap so we all have the same checklist and a few concrete asks so we can size a proposal: 

What I captured during the call (please correct if I missed anything):
- Primary traffic pattern: infrequent steady traffic + short bursts tied to batch jobs and campaign sends.
- Expected steady-state QPS: small (single digits) during daytime business hours.
- Peak bursts: short spikes up to 80–140 QPS for 30–90s during campaign triggers.
- Typical tokens per request: ~350–600 (user prompt + context).
- Streaming: yes — UX streams partial tokens to the web client; chunk size roughly ~64 tokens, they want end-to-end perceptible latency under ~300ms for most chunks.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile token latency target around 250–300ms; p50 much lower.
- Concurrency: user-facing concurrency target ~60 active connections during peak.

As next steps from our side if you confirm the numbers above:
1) Olivia: confirm the steady vs peak QPS numbers and whether 140 QPS is a hard upper bound or theoretical max.
2) Alex: draft initial throughput plan and model choices for a dedicated or hosted route.
3) Ops ask (Neha/Priyom): run a quick back-of-envelope for required GPU pool size given streaming and token-per-second targets.
4) Schedule a 30-min technical deep dive (optional) to validate chunking and client retry behavior.

I attached a very small worksheet and token distribution sample to help illustrate how we convert tokens/sec and QPS into GPU slots. Will iterate once you confirm the numbers.

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Attachment: throughput-plan-draft.xlsx (xlsx - draft sizing sheet)
Attachment: token-distribution.csv (csv - anonymized sample)
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@vendipay.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: VendiPay Platform Team <platform@vendipay.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 11:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & asks: burst profile, streaming constraints, and next steps

Thanks Alex — appreciate the clear notes. Confirming / clarifying: 
- Steady-state QPS: ~8 QPS (95% of work is low-volume background inference).
- Peak bursts: nominally up to ~120 QPS; we've seen transient spikes as high as 150 QPS during big campaigns but they last <2 minutes. For sizing we'd treat 120 QPS as expected peak and 150 QPS as extreme.
- Tokens per request: median ~420, 90th ~900 (we've attached a heatmap offline — sharing in the Drive).
- Streaming: yes — client relies on streaming for UX. Chunk size today is roughly 50–80 tokens; acceptable chunk latency is 200–300ms for 90% of chunks.
- Latency SLO: ideally p95 token latency < 250ms; absolute hard requirement is p95 < 400ms.
- Concurrency: during marketing bursts ~65 concurrent conversational sessions; outside bursts ~8–12.
- Retry tolerance: clients will retry on 5xx/backoff; useful to keep errors <1% during peaks.

Happy for you to propose a mix of dedicated pool + fallbacks to hosted for extremes. We can do the 30-min technical call on Thursday if that helps.

Olivia Chen
Head of Platform Infrastructure
VendiPay
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@vendipay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & asks: burst profile, streaming constraints, and next steps

Thanks for the clarifications — that helps a lot, Olivia. Action & proposal snapshot: 

Short plan (what we'll deliver next):
- Draft capacity plan that maps: steady QPS (~8), expected peak (120), and protection for extremes (150) into GPU slot count and expected token/sec headroom.
- Streaming-safe configuration: continuous batching disabled for UX-critical routes; small batch window (~10ms) for throughput-friendly fallbacks; KV cache retention tuned for session affinity.
- Model recommendation: r-instruct-7b-q4 or r-chat-13b-q4 for higher-quality replies; we'll include per-token cost estimates.
- Fallback policy: route to hosted spikes when dedicated pool saturation exceeds 80%; healthy circuit-breaker defaults.

Neha / Priyom — can you validate these rough assumptions against our sizing guide:
- 120 QPS at median 420 tokens/request => ~50k tokens/sec sustained during peak bursts (rough calc: 120 * 420 = 50,400).
- Streaming constraints mean we should prioritize low-latency kernels and smaller batch windows — likely increases required GPU slots by ~20% vs batch-optimized configs.

I've attached the draft worksheet and token sample (same as before) — please update the sizing sheet directly with any revised throughput multipliers.

If the 30-min technical call works for you Olivia, how about Thursday 2027-06-03 15:00 PT? Otherwise we can do Friday morning.

Cheers,
Alex

Attachment: throughput-plan-draft.xlsx
Attachment: token-distribution.csv
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: VendiPay sizing ask — quick ops checklist

Internal notes / asks (short):
- Confirm Alex's back-of-envelope: 120 QPS * 420 tokens/request -> ~50.4k tokens/sec at peak. Convert into GPU slots: assume r-instruct-7b-q4 performance baseline ~8k tokens/sec per slot for low-latency streaming profile => ~7 slots (ceiling -> 8), plus +20% headroom -> 10 slots.
- If customer picks r-chat-13b-q4, expected token/sec per slot drops (~4k tokens/sec) -> need ~13 slots + 20% headroom -> ~16.
- Verify whether we can reserve a small dedicated pool (10 slots) with burst-to-hosted up to 150 QPS.
- Ops checklist for candidate dedicated: autoscale cooldowns, fallback route, cache warming policy, tracing hooks enabled for p95 token latency measurement.

Priyom: can you run the quick perf table and confirm the per-slot token/sec numbers for the two model candidates? Neha: flag any ops constraints for streaming (kernel selection, batch windows, TCP keepalive tweaks).

I'll lock the Thursday tech call if Olivia confirms.

— Alex
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
